title: Strict-local projective-line exchange
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be a local morphism of strictly henselian local rings inducing a
specified extension of their separably closed residue fields. For the
base-change square of $\mathbf P^1_A\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, the stalk of the
exchange morphism [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] at the closed geometric
point of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is the restriction map between the
cohomologies of the two closed projective lines. If the residue-field map is
an isomorphism, this stalk map is an isomorphism.

proof.text: For the projective-line square obtain a1,a2 identifying stalk exchange with cohomology pullback on the two total projective lines, with no closed-fibre comparison used yet.

The residue-field identity Res(phi) after res(A) = res(B) after phi gives a commuting square of projective lines by contravariance of Spec.map and ProjectiveSpace.map_comp. Stalks of inverse images equal the original stalks, so torsion is preserved (the existing instance isTorsionSheaf_upperStar). Apply the strictly henselian projective-line comparison over A to F and over B to g prime inverse image of F. These are the two bijective restriction hypotheses of the restriction-square transport theorem. Obtain b1,b2 and its commuting equation.

Define e1=a1 followed by b1 and e2=a2 followed by b2. Rewrite first with the total-space exchange equation, then with the restriction-square equation. This proves the unchanged existential statement. The existing second assertion then follows from bijectivity of pullback along an isomorphism of residue fields.
